name: Meissner wall
description:
Three interlocking name walls, with recessed front lettering and plain, unnumbered backs. The 5.0 mm studs were physically tested with good clutch. Lettering recesses are 0.6 mm deep, leaving 0.9 mm of front wall.
Meissner: 12 studs wide, 3 bricks high, 2 studs deep. Ten bricks in staggered rows of 4+4+4, 2+4+4+2, 4+4+4 studs. Body 95.8 x 15.8 x 28.8 mm; 30.6 mm including top studs.
Käte: 6 studs wide, 2 bricks high, 2 studs deep. Four bricks in staggered rows of 4+2 and 2+4 studs. Body 47.8 x 15.8 x 19.2 mm; 21 mm including top studs. Both umlaut dots are included.
Carlo: 8 studs wide, 2 bricks high, 2 studs deep. Five bricks in staggered rows of 4+4 and 2+4+2 studs. Body 63.8 x 15.8 x 19.2 mm; 21 mm including top studs. The print plate has six separate pieces: one complete plain wall plus an alternative upper-left corner with a 5 mm key-ring passage connecting the center of the left face to the center of the body top. The bent passage has an internal reinforcing sleeve and preserves the top studs and lower clutch area. The assembled preview shows the plain wall on the left and key-ring wall on the right; shared parts only need to be printed once.
Print the corresponding meissner-wall.stl, kate-wall.stl or carlo-wall.stl. Split the plate into objects in the slicer to extract any individual brick for reprinting. Separate single-brick STL downloads are omitted for all three variants. Files containing combined are previews only. Use 100% scale, studs up, open undersides on the bed, supports and internal brims off, and 0.12-0.16 mm layers. Key-ring fit, passage print quality and attachment strength still need a physical test.
